item.title: Indian-origin teen built anti-cyberbullying tech in 2013; now runs non-profit rewarded by Prince Harry and Meghan Markle
item.description: Trisha Prabhu created ReThink, a mobile keyboard preventing cyberbullying by prompting users to reconsider offensive messages. This initiative grew into a global non-profit organization supporting millions of students worldwide. Prabhu's work earned her significant recognition and substantial funding for her impactful efforts. She continues to lead ReThink Citizens, promoting digital wellness and a kinder internet. Her dedication exemplifies how one motivated individual can drive significant positive social change.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Women were barred from Liechtenstein’s throne for 400 years; new rule lets the firstborn inherit regardless of gender
item.description: Liechtenstein has made a progressive move by updating its royal succession laws to favor gender equality. Now, the first-born child will inherit the throne, breaking traditional norms. This decision aligns with several European countries where female heirs are already established, like Great Britain, which pioneered similar reforms in 2011. Meanwhile, Japan still grapples with its frustrating male-only inheritance policy that raises many questions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Black drongos introduced for pest control later threatened Guam’s native birds
item.description: In 1935, the introduction of black drongos to Rota aimed to control agricultural pests. This effort led to the birds establishing their populations, eventually spreading to Guam. However, their aggressive behavior towards native bird species has contributed significantly to declines in local avian populations, highlighting the unforeseen consequences of introducing non-native species into ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: ‘No intention to attack N Korea’: S Korea Prez Lee after Trump reduces US drills
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung advocates for stronger independent defense capabilities. He defended annual civil-defense exercises as purely defensive measures. These drills occur alongside joint US-South Korea military exercises. President Trump previously instructed the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military drills. Seoul plans to continue strengthening its own defense while maintaining its alliance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A rare orca known as “La Abuela” was found with wounds consistent with shotgun pellets; could threaten an entire Iberian population of fewer than 40 whales
item.description: Spain's Environment Ministry is actively investigating a distressing situation involving Toni, an injured Iberian orca. The oldest member of her pod has been discovered with wounds resembling those inflicted by shotgun pellets, as witnessed by marine conservationists documenting several impacts on her dorsal fin. The Iberian orca population is critically endangered and endures significant threats due to human actions and pollution.

item.title: 5,000-year-old Japanese pot in New York has a flame-like rim
item.description: The Kaen doki, an ancient Japanese pot, carries a history that spans millennia. Distinct in its design, featuring a flame-like mouth and cord-marked details, this earthenware piece exemplifies the craftsmanship of Jomon potters. Built from carefully shaped clay coils with pierced openings, this stunning artifact is a glimpse into the artistic achievements of the past and now resides proudly in The Metropolitan Museum of Art.

item.title: Princess Eugenie reveals baby daughter’s name with touching tribute to Queen Elizabeth II
item.description: Princess Eugenie has revealed the name of her newborn daughter with a touching tribute to the late Queen Elizabeth II. Eugenie and Jack Brooksbank have named their third child Adelaide Elizabeth Annina Brooksbank. The royal said the name honours three people they love and admire, while also reflecting their connection to England and Portugal.

item.title: ‘I cannot walk, I use two crutches’: 85-year-old Rochford man told to remove £2,200 driveway
item.description: An 85-year-old Rochford man is facing the threat of legal action after being ordered to remove a £2,200 block-paved driveway he built on a grass verge outside his home. David Siggins, who uses two crutches and has COPD, says he was given permission to build it but has now been told the land belongs to Rochford Council.

item.title: President Donald Trump tells 10-year-old rescued by teen lifeguard he “wouldn’t” have risked his life to save him
item.description: In a remarkable display of courage, 16-year-old lifeguard Ryder Williams saved Nathanial Rai, a young boy, from perilous waters at the California beach. Their heroic rescue, which gained significant attention after going viral, caught the eye of President Donald Trump, who invited both to the White House. Williams emphasized his rigorous training and swift action during the rescue, sparking conversations about lifeguards' official recognition as first responders.

item.title: Meet 17-year-old Tiya Aggarwal, who built a smart watering system for 150+ plant species
item.description: Canadian high school student Tiya Aggarwal has won the top prize at a British Columbia entrepreneurship competition for Aquora150, a smart irrigation system designed to automatically adjust care for more than 150 plant species. The system uses humidity-capturing technology to hydrate houseplants while reducing water, plastic and glass waste.

item.title: US Supreme Court again rejects Trump's bid to overturn $5mn E Jean Carroll verdict
item.description: The US Supreme Court again rejected Donald Trump's attempt to overturn a civil verdict. A jury had previously found him liable for sexual abuse and defamation against E. Jean Carroll. This decision leaves a $5 million judgment in place, which Trump has now paid. Another separate $83.3 million verdict against Trump is still pending before the Supreme Court.
